Cashew anthracnose.name: Anthracnose
Cashew anthracnose.description: A serious fungal disease causing dark, sunken lesions on leaves, twigs, and nuts of cashew trees.

treatments.title: Copper Fungicide
treatments.desc: Apply Bordeaux mixture (1%) or copper oxychloride spray at 15-day intervals during the rainy season.

treatments.title: Neem Oil Spray
treatments.desc: Spray 3% neem oil solution as a preventive measure. Repeat every 10-14 days.

treatments.title: Pruning
treatments.desc: Remove and destroy infected twigs and branches to reduce fungal inoculum.

treatments.title: Trichoderma
treatments.desc: Apply Trichoderma-based biocontrol agent to the soil around the tree base.

Cashew anthracnose.prevention: Maintain proper spacing, prune for air circulation, and avoid water stagnation.

Cashew gumosis.name: Gummosis
Cashew gumosis.description: A condition where gum oozes from the bark of cashew trees, often caused by fungal or bacterial infection.

treatments.title: Wound Treatment
treatments.desc: Clean the affected area and apply Bordeaux paste (10%) on the wounds.

treatments.title: Copper Spray
treatments.desc: Spray copper oxychloride (0.3%) on the trunk and main branches.

treatments.title: Neem Cake
treatments.desc: Apply neem cake around the tree base to suppress soil-borne pathogens.

treatments.title: Proper Drainage
treatments.desc: Ensure proper drainage around the tree to prevent waterlogging.

Cashew gumosis.prevention: Avoid mechanical injuries, maintain tree vigor with balanced nutrition.

Cashew healthy.name: Healthy
Cashew healthy.description: Your cashew plant looks healthy with no visible signs of disease or pest damage.

treatments.title: Regular Monitoring
treatments.desc: Continue monitoring for early signs of disease, especially during rainy season.

treatments.title: Balanced Nutrition
treatments.desc: Apply organic compost and micronutrients for sustained health.

Cashew leaf miner.name: Leaf Miner
Cashew leaf miner.description: Larvae of leaf miner insects tunnel through cashew leaves, creating serpentine mines and reducing photosynthesis.

treatments.title: Neem Oil
treatments.desc: Spray 2-3% neem oil solution to deter egg-laying and kill larvae.

treatments.title: Sticky Traps
treatments.desc: Install yellow sticky traps to monitor and capture adult leaf miners.

treatments.title: Biological Control
treatments.desc: Encourage natural predators like parasitic wasps (Chrysonotomyia spp.).

treatments.title: Remove Affected Leaves
treatments.desc: Hand-pick and destroy heavily mined leaves to reduce population.

Cashew leaf miner.prevention: Maintain tree health, use neem as preventive spray.

Cashew red rust.name: Red Rust
Cashew red rust.description: An algal disease caused by Cephaleuros virescens, creating rusty-red patches on cashew leaves and stems.

treatments.title: Copper Fungicide
treatments.desc: Spray Bordeaux mixture (1%) or copper hydroxide at first sign of infection.

treatments.title: Pruning
treatments.desc: Prune affected branches to improve air circulation and light penetration.

treatments.title: Oil Spray
treatments.desc: Apply horticultural oil spray to suffocate the algal growth.

Cashew red rust.prevention: Ensure adequate spacing and sunlight exposure for trees.

Cassava bacterial blight.name: Bacterial Blight
Cassava bacterial blight.description: A devastating bacterial disease causing angular leaf spots, wilting, and stem dieback in cassava.

treatments.title: Resistant Varieties
treatments.desc: Plant resistant or tolerant cassava varieties (e.g., TME 419, IITA varieties).

treatments.title: Clean Planting Material
treatments.desc: Use only disease-free stem cuttings from healthy plants.

treatments.title: Copper Spray
treatments.desc: Apply copper-based bactericides as a preventive measure during planting.

treatments.title: Roguing
treatments.desc: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately to prevent spread.

Cassava bacterial blight.prevention: Use certified disease-free planting material, practice crop rotation.

Cassava brown spot.name: Brown Spot
Cassava brown spot.description: A fungal leaf spot disease causing small brown circular spots on cassava leaves.

treatments.title: Neem Extract
treatments.desc: Spray neem leaf extract (5%) on affected plants weekly.

treatments.title: Improve Nutrition
treatments.desc: Apply organic compost to boost plant immunity.

treatments.title: Remove Debris
treatments.desc: Clean up fallen leaves and plant debris around cassava plants.

Cassava brown spot.prevention: Maintain soil fertility and proper plant spacing.

Cassava green mite.name: Green Mite
Cassava green mite.description: Tiny green mites that feed on cassava leaves, causing chlorosis and leaf distortion, especially in dry conditions.
symptoms: Tiny green dots on leaf undersides

treatments.title: Predatory Mites
treatments.desc: Release Typhlodromalus aripo (predatory mite) as biological control.

treatments.title: Neem Oil
treatments.desc: Spray 2% neem oil to suffocate mites. Cover leaf undersides thoroughly.

treatments.title: Water Spray
treatments.desc: Strong water jets can dislodge mites from leaves.

treatments.title: Sulfur Spray
treatments.desc: Apply organic wettable sulfur spray as a miticide.

Cassava green mite.prevention: Plant during rainy season, use resistant varieties, maintain soil moisture.

Cassava healthy.name: Healthy
Cassava healthy.description: Your cassava plant is healthy with no visible disease or pest damage.

treatments.title: Regular Monitoring
treatments.desc: Continue checking leaves regularly, especially during dry season.

treatments.title: Mulching
treatments.desc: Apply organic mulch to conserve soil moisture and suppress weeds.

Cassava mosaic.name: Mosaic Disease
Cassava mosaic.description: A viral disease spread by whiteflies causing mosaic patterns, leaf distortion, and severe yield loss.

treatments.title: Resistant Varieties
treatments.desc: Plant CMD-resistant varieties (e.g., TME 419, UMUCASS series).

treatments.title: Whitefly Control
treatments.desc: Use yellow sticky traps and neem oil sprays to control whitefly vectors.

treatments.title: Roguing
treatments.desc: Remove and destroy infected plants within the first 3 months after planting.

treatments.title: Clean Cuttings
treatments.desc: Source planting material only from disease-free mother plants.

Cassava mosaic.prevention: Use certified clean planting material, control whitefly populations.

Maize fall armyworm.name: Fall Armyworm
Maize fall armyworm.description: A highly destructive pest whose larvae feed voraciously on maize leaves, whorls, and ears.

treatments.title: Bt Spray
treatments.desc: Apply Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) spray targeting young larvae in the whorl.

treatments.title: Neem Extract
treatments.desc: Apply 5% neem seed kernel extract directly into the whorl early morning.

treatments.title: Trichogramma
treatments.desc: Release Trichogramma parasitoid wasps for egg parasitism.

treatments.title: Ash + Sand
treatments.desc: Mix wood ash with fine sand and apply into the whorl to desiccate larvae.

Maize fall armyworm.prevention: Early planting, intercropping with legumes, maintain field hygiene.

Maize grasshoper.name: Grasshopper Damage
Maize grasshoper.description: Grasshoppers feeding on maize leaves and stems, causing defoliation and reduced grain fill.

treatments.title: Neem Oil
treatments.desc: Spray concentrated neem oil (3-5%) to deter feeding and disrupt molting.

treatments.title: Garlic Spray
treatments.desc: Blend garlic with water and spray as a natural repellent.

treatments.title: Nosema Bait
treatments.desc: Use Nosema locustae bait for biological grasshopper control.

treatments.title: Physical Barriers
treatments.desc: Use row covers on young plants during peak grasshopper season.

Maize grasshoper.prevention: Remove weeds around field edges, encourage natural predators (birds, spiders).

Maize healthy.name: Healthy
Maize healthy.description: Your maize plant looks healthy with good growth and no visible disease or pest damage.

treatments.title: Continue Care
treatments.desc: Maintain consistent watering and balanced organic fertilization.

treatments.title: Weed Management
treatments.desc: Keep field weed-free, especially during the first 6 weeks.

Maize leaf beetle.name: Leaf Beetle
Maize leaf beetle.description: Beetles and their larvae feed on maize leaves and roots, causing skeletonization and reduced vigor.

treatments.title: Neem Oil
treatments.desc: Spray 2% neem oil on affected plants to repel adults and kill larvae.

treatments.title: Kaolin Clay
treatments.desc: Apply kaolin clay spray to create a physical barrier on leaves.

treatments.title: Hand Picking
treatments.desc: Manually remove adult beetles in small fields early morning when they are sluggish.

treatments.title: Crop Rotation
treatments.desc: Rotate with non-host crops to break the beetle life cycle.

Maize leaf beetle.prevention: Practice crop rotation and maintain clean field borders.

Maize leaf blight.name: Leaf Blight
Maize leaf blight.description: A destructive fungal disease causing long, grayish-green to tan lesions on maize leaves.

treatments.title: Trichoderma
treatments.desc: Apply Trichoderma-based foliar spray at early symptom appearance.

treatments.title: Copper Fungicide
treatments.desc: Use organic copper fungicide as a preventive during humid weather.

treatments.title: Residue Management
treatments.desc: Destroy or deeply plow infected crop residue after harvest.

treatments.title: Resistant Hybrids
treatments.desc: Plant blight-resistant maize hybrids for future seasons.

Maize leaf blight.prevention: Rotate crops, manage residue, use resistant varieties.

Maize leaf spot.name: Leaf Spot
Maize leaf spot.description: Small, circular to oval spots on maize leaves caused by various fungi.

treatments.title: Compost Tea
treatments.desc: Spray aerated compost tea to boost leaf microbiome and suppress pathogens.

treatments.title: Baking Soda Spray
treatments.desc: Mix 1 tbsp baking soda in 1 gallon water with a drop of soap. Spray weekly.

treatments.title: Improve Spacing
treatments.desc: Ensure adequate plant spacing for better air circulation.

Maize leaf spot.prevention: Maintain balanced nutrition and avoid excessive nitrogen.

Maize streak virus.name: Streak Virus
Maize streak virus.description: A viral disease transmitted by leafhoppers, causing characteristic yellow streaks along leaf veins.
symptoms: Yellow streaks parallel to leaf veins
Plants may die if infected early

treatments.title: Vector Control
treatments.desc: Control leafhopper vectors with neem oil or pyrethrin sprays.

treatments.title: Remove Infected Plants
treatments.desc: Rogue out infected plants early to reduce virus source.

treatments.title: Resistant Varieties
treatments.desc: Plant MSV-resistant maize varieties (essential in endemic areas).

treatments.title: Early Planting
treatments.desc: Plant early in the season to avoid peak leafhopper populations.

Maize streak virus.prevention: Use resistant varieties, control vectors, eliminate grass weeds that harbor virus.

Tomato healthy.name: Healthy
Tomato healthy.description: Your tomato plant is healthy and thriving! No signs of disease or pest damage.

treatments.title: Maintain Watering
treatments.desc: Keep a consistent watering schedule — 1-2 inches per week.

treatments.title: Organic Compost
treatments.desc: Feed with balanced organic compost every 2-3 weeks.

treatments.title: Mulch
treatments.desc: Apply organic mulch to retain moisture and suppress weeds.

Tomato leaf blight.name: Leaf Blight
Tomato leaf blight.description: A fungal disease causing large brown lesions on tomato leaves, leading to rapid defoliation.
symptoms: White fuzzy growth in humid conditions

treatments.title: Remove Infected Tissue
treatments.desc: Immediately remove and destroy affected leaves and stems.

treatments.title: Copper Fungicide
treatments.desc: Apply copper hydroxide or Bordeaux mixture preventatively.

treatments.title: Bacillus Subtilis
treatments.desc: Spray Serenade (Bacillus subtilis) as an organic biocontrol.

treatments.title: Improve Air Flow
treatments.desc: Stake and prune plants for better air circulation.

Tomato leaf blight.prevention: Water at base, avoid overhead irrigation, use resistant varieties.

Tomato leaf curl.name: Leaf Curl Virus
Tomato leaf curl.description: A devastating viral disease spread by whiteflies, causing upward curling and yellowing of tomato leaves.

treatments.title: Whitefly Control
treatments.desc: Use yellow sticky traps and neem oil sprays to control whitefly vectors.

treatments.title: Reflective Mulch
treatments.desc: Use silver reflective mulch to repel whiteflies from the crop.

treatments.title: Remove Infected Plants
treatments.desc: Rogue out infected plants immediately to prevent virus spread.

treatments.title: Resistant Varieties
treatments.desc: Plant ToLCV-resistant tomato varieties.

Tomato leaf curl.prevention: Control whiteflies early, use resistant varieties, maintain field hygiene.

Tomato septoria leaf spot.name: Septoria Leaf Spot
Tomato septoria leaf spot.description: A common fungal disease causing small circular spots with dark borders and tan centers on tomato leaves.
symptoms: Small circular spots with dark borders
Tan/gray centers with tiny dark specks

treatments.title: Copper Spray
treatments.desc: Apply copper-based organic fungicide at first sign of spots.

treatments.title: Baking Soda Spray
treatments.desc: Mix 1 tbsp baking soda + liquid soap in 1 gallon water. Spray weekly.

treatments.title: Mulching
treatments.desc: Apply thick mulch to prevent soil splash spreading spores to leaves.

treatments.title: Remove Lower Leaves
treatments.desc: Prune the bottom 12 inches of foliage to prevent soil contact.

Tomato septoria leaf spot.prevention: Rotate crops for 3 years, clean up debris, avoid overhead watering.

Tomato verticulium wilt.name: Verticillium Wilt
Tomato verticulium wilt.description: A soil-borne fungal disease causing one-sided wilting and yellowing of tomato plants.

treatments.title: Solarization
treatments.desc: Cover moist soil with clear plastic for 4-6 weeks to kill fungal spores via solar heat.

treatments.title: Trichoderma
treatments.desc: Apply Trichoderma harzianum to soil before planting as biocontrol.

treatments.title: Resistant Varieties
treatments.desc: Plant Verticillium-resistant varieties (look for 'V' on seed labels).

treatments.title: Crop Rotation
treatments.desc: Rotate with non-solanaceous crops for at least 4 years.

Tomato verticulium wilt.prevention: Use resistant varieties, solarize soil, maintain balanced nutrition.
